name: document_landmarks
description: Extract compact document landmarks for retrieval indexing (abstract, glossary, executive_summary, etc.). The user content is composed of the document file name, document style, and the JSON-serialized list of candidate pages. Returns JSON with top-level 'landmarks' array.
system: You extract compact document landmarks for retrieval indexing.
user:
You identify durable document landmarks for long-document retrieval.
Return JSON with top-level key 'landmarks'. Each item must include:
- landmark_type: one of abstract, acknowledgements, author_correspondence, definition_region, executive_summary, foreword, glossary, preface, title_page, volume_boundary
- title: short label
- page_label: page where the landmark appears
- summary: concise description of what the page/region contains
- key_value_facts: array of short factual strings visible in the supplied text, such as author, contact, signature, version, definition, volume scope, or funding facts
- source_snippet: exact short snippet from supplied text supporting the landmark
- confidence: number between 0 and 1
Rules:
- Create only landmarks supported by supplied page text.
- Do not infer facts from outside the text.
- Prefer no landmark over a vague landmark.
- Use definition_region or glossary for acronym/definition-heavy regions.
- Use author_correspondence for author, affiliation, contact, or corresponding-author blocks.
- Use foreword/preface/title_page/executive_summary/abstract/volume_boundary only when the supplied text supports that region type.
Document: {{file_name}}
Document style: {{document_style}}
Candidate pages: {{candidate_pages_json}}
notes: Pre-registry source: src/landmarks/service.py::DocumentLandmarkService._prompt. The candidate_pages JSON is built from the per-page payload (page_label, section_heading, section_kind, section_path, candidate_reasons, cleaned text). Used at indexing time only — no /qa path.
